newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' San Miguel reports weak 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' San Miguel reports weak 1996 results.

text.p: San Miguel Corp, the biggest brewery in the Philippines, reported weak but slightly better than expected financial results for 1996 on Wednesday and said that it would post higher earnings this year.

The food and drink conglomerate, which also has operations in Hong Kong, China, Vietnam, Taiwan and Indonesia, said net profit in 1996 rose to 6.09 billion pesos ($231.558 million) from 5.84 billion pesos in 1995, but added that the figures included one-time gains.
Net of one-time gains, earnings dropped to 5.26 billion pesos from 5.38 billion pesos in 1995, a 2.0 percent fall.
But analysts said the figures were within forecasts or marginally better than expected.
"There were no surprises. The figures were generally within expectations," said Jonas Ferrer, vice president for research at Pryce Securities.
Analysts said they expected the beer-based conglomerate to either report weaker or flat earnings this year, and a modest recovery in 1997.
A Reuters poll of seven Manila brokerages earlier in the month had placed the company's net profits minus one-time gains at an average 5.22 billion pesos in 1996 and at 6.05 billion pesos in 1997.
"The net income was slightly positive and not as bad as envisioned by most brokerage houses," said Wilfred Son Keng Po, chief operating officer at Angping Securities.
"The 1996 San Miguel income figure was better as it was a little higher (than our) forecast of five billion pesos," said Helen Alvarez, research head of All Asia Securities.
Analysts attributed the weak earnings of San Miguel in 1996 to high raw materials costs and the burden of funding overseas expansion.
San Miguel said the operating income of its beverage segment dropped by two percent to 8.34 billion pesos mainly due to losses in the company's international beer brewing operations.
But it said it expected 1997 to be better.
"1997 earnings are expected to exhibit significant growth. Marketing and distribution programmes are aimed at increasing volumes by over 10 percent," San Miguel said in a statement.
It had earlier said 1996 sales had increased to 85 billion pesos from 76.6 billion pesos in 1995.
The company also expects to benefit from various actions taken in the past year to make its operations more efficient, cost competitive and responsive to the market, it said.
Last year, San Miguel spent money on various expansion projects, including four overseas breweries.
As a result, financing charges jumped by 92 percent to 2.64 billion pesos from 1.38 billion pesos, San Miguel said.
All Asia's Alvarez said the A shares of San Miguel, open to Filipinos only, were still a buy after closing on Wednesday at 55.50 pesos or at 19 times projected earnings in 1997.
The B shares, open to local and foreign investors, were fully valued 105 pesos, or 39 times the projected 1997 net income, she said.
Similar food and beverage issues at the Philippine Stock Exchange were trading at 22 times their projected 1997 earnings, Alvarez said.
